narrative.overview: BlockFactor is an analytical, high-density location intelligence system engineered to deliver objective residential livability assessments for Chicago. The interface models a tactical urban control room: crisp dark zinc surfaces, strict 1px border delineation, authentic municipal CTA line badges, and monospace tabular telemetry. It rejects generic marketing froth in favor of raw informational density and mathematical clarity.
keyCharacteristics: Tactical high-density information architecture prioritizing metrics, entity names, and exact distances
Flat tonal layering (deep zinc-950 canvas, zinc-900 surfaces, zinc-800 borders, zero drop shadows)
Strict data typography: Geist Mono for all numeric scores, coordinates, distances, and transit durations
Authentic municipal color palette anchored in official CTA transit line hues
Zero AI novelty clichés (no purple neon gradients, no sparkle icons, no emoji slop)

rules.name: The Tabular Monospace Rule
rules.body: Every coordinate, distance, travel duration, and calculated score must render in Geist Mono with tabular lining figures to ensure zero visual jitter during live updates.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are strictly flat with no drop shadows; visual hierarchy and elevation are conveyed exclusively through tonal stepping (zinc-950 → zinc-900 → zinc-800) and 1px border strokes.

rules.name: The Authentic Transit Palette Rule
rules.body: Transit badges and line indicators must use exact Chicago CTA hex codes (Red, Blue, Brown, Green, Pink, Orange, Purple, Yellow); never approximate or theme-shift official municipal lines.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Accent colors appear strictly on badges, score tiers, and map overlays. Surfaces and containers remain strictly neutral zinc to preserve high contrast and scanability.

dos: Do use Geist Mono for all numeric scores, distances, coordinates, and travel durations
Do use exact CTA transit line colors for route badges, transit chips, and map layers
Do maintain tight border radii (rounded-sm 2px for cards and badges)
Do lead component copy with metrics, entity names, and straight-line distances
Do maintain 1px zinc-800 borders between tonal surfaces for crisp visual delineation
donts: Don't use drop shadows, glow filters, or floating elevated surfaces
Don't use emojis in metric cards, table headers, scorecards, or empty states
Don't use purple or violet radial background glows or AI novelty tropes
Don't write redundant explanatory fluff subtitles under score headers
Don't approximate CTA transit line colors with generic Tailwind accents
